namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Chains (§40, §42, §49) -/

/-- A chain from an element without link is empty (§40 parents, §42 origins). -/
theorem chainF_none {org : Nat → Option Nat} {i : Nat} (h : org i = none) :
    ∀ k, chainF org k i = []
  | 0 => rfl
  | _ + 1 => by simp [chainF, h]

/-- Any fuel at least the start index gives the same chain (§40, §42; acyclicity, §49). -/
theorem chainF_fuel (org : Nat → Option Nat) :
    ∀ k₁ k₂ i, i ≤ k₁ → i ≤ k₂ → chainF org k₁ i = chainF org k₂ i
  | 0, 0, _, _, _ => rfl
  | 0, _ + 1, i, h, _ => by
    obtain rfl : i = 0 := by omega
    simp only [chainF]; split <;> simp
  | _ + 1, 0, i, _, h => by
    obtain rfl : i = 0 := by omega
    simp only [chainF]; split <;> simp
  | k₁ + 1, k₂ + 1, i, h₁, h₂ => by
    simp only [chainF]; split
    · split
      · rw [chainF_fuel org k₁ k₂ _ (by omega) (by omega)]
      · rfl
    · rfl

/-- The chain of an element without link is empty (§40, §42). -/
theorem chain_none {org : Nat → Option Nat} {i : Nat} (h : org i = none) : chain org i = [] :=
  chainF_none h i

/-- The chain of `i` is its link followed by the chain of the link (§40, §42). -/
theorem chain_cons {org : Nat → Option Nat} {i o : Nat} (h : org i = some o) (hlt : o < i) :
    chain org i = o :: chain org o := by
  obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ : ∃ k, i = k + 1 := ⟨i - 1, by omega⟩
  simp only [chain, chainF, h, hlt, ↓reduceIte]
  rw [chainF_fuel org k o o (by omega) (Nat.le_refl o)]

/-- Elements of a chain are below its start (§49, acyclic chains). -/
theorem chainF_lt {org : Nat → Option Nat} : ∀ k i j, j ∈ chainF org k i → j < i
  | 0, _, _, h => by simp [chainF] at h
  | k + 1, i, j, h => by
    simp only [chainF] at h; split at h
    · split at h
      · rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h
        · assumption
        · exact Nat.lt_trans (chainF_lt k _ j h) ‹_›
      · simp at h
    · simp at h

/-- Every element of a chain is below its start (§49, acyclic chains). -/
theorem chain_lt {org : Nat → Option Nat} {i j : Nat} (h : j ∈ chain org i) : j < i :=
  chainF_lt i i j h

/-- A chain within fuel `k` has at most `k` elements (§49, finite chains). -/
theorem chainF_length {org : Nat → Option Nat} : ∀ k i, (chainF org k i).length ≤ k
  | 0, _ => by simp [chainF]
  | k + 1, i => by
    simp only [chainF]; split
    · split
      · simp only [List.length_cons]; have := chainF_length (org := org) k ‹_›; omega
      · simp
    · simp

/-- A chain from `i` has at most `i` elements (§49, finite chains). -/
theorem chain_length (org : Nat → Option Nat) (i : Nat) : (chain org i).length ≤ i :=
  chainF_length i i

/-- A chain depends only on the links at or below its start (§40, §42). -/
theorem chainF_congr {org org' : Nat → Option Nat} :
    ∀ k i, (∀ j ≤ i, org j = org' j) → chainF org k i = chainF org' k i
  | 0, _, _ => rfl
  | k + 1, i, h => by
    simp only [chainF]; rw [h i (Nat.le_refl i)]; split
    · split
      · rw [chainF_congr k _ fun j hj => h j (by omega)]
      · rfl
    · rfl

/-- A chain depends only on the links at or below its start (§40, §42). -/
theorem chain_congr {org org' : Nat → Option Nat} {i : Nat} (h : ∀ j ≤ i, org j = org' j) :
    chain org i = chain org' i := chainF_congr i i h

/-- Two elements without link of one chain are equal (§40 root places, §49.5 root
authorities). -/
theorem chainF_root {org : Nat → Option Nat} : ∀ k i r r', r ∈ chainF org k i → org r = none →
    r' ∈ chainF org k i → org r' = none → r = r'
  | 0, _, _, _, h, _, _, _ => by simp [chainF] at h
  | k + 1, i, r, r', h, hr, h', hr' => by
    simp only [chainF] at h h'; split at h
    · rename_i o ho; simp only [ho] at h'
      split at h
      · rename_i hlt; simp only [hlt, ↓reduceIte] at h'
        rcases List.mem_cons.1 h with rfl | h <;> rcases List.mem_cons.1 h' with rfl | h'
        · rfl
        · rw [chainF_none hr] at h'; simp at h'
        · rw [chainF_none hr'] at h; simp at h
        · exact chainF_root k _ r r' h hr h' hr'
      · simp at h
    · simp at h

/-- A chain contains the chain of each of its elements, for links to smaller indices (§40, §42,
§49). -/
theorem chain_trans {org : Nat → Option Nat} (hlt : ∀ i o, org i = some o → o < i) :
    ∀ n i, i < n → ∀ r, r ∈ chain org i → ∀ o ∈ chain org r, o ∈ chain org i
  | 0, _, h, _, _, _, _ => absurd h (Nat.not_lt_zero _)
  | n + 1, i, hi, r, hr, o, ho => by
    cases hp : org i with
    | none => rw [chain_none hp] at hr; simp at hr
    | some p =>
      have hpi := hlt i p hp
      rw [chain_cons hp hpi] at hr ⊢
      rcases List.mem_cons.1 hr with rfl | hr
      · exact List.mem_cons_of_mem _ ho
      · exact List.mem_cons_of_mem _ (chain_trans hlt n p (by omega) r hr o ho)

/-- An element of a chain is the link of the start or belongs to the chain of that link (§40,
§42). -/
theorem mem_chain {org : Nat → Option Nat} {i x : Nat} (h : x ∈ chain org i) :
    ∃ o, org i = some o ∧ o < i ∧ (x = o ∨ x ∈ chain org o) := by
  cases ho : org i with
  | none => rw [chain_none ho] at h; simp at h
  | some o =>
    rcases Nat.lt_or_ge o i with hlt | hge
    · rw [chain_cons ho hlt] at h; exact ⟨o, rfl, hlt, List.mem_cons.1 h⟩
    · exfalso
      cases i with
      | zero => simp [chain, chainF] at h
      | succ k => simp [chain, chainF, ho, Nat.not_lt.2 hge] at h

/-! ## Footprints and frames of places (§40) -/

/-- Membership in `footprint(q)` (§40): an existing leaf that is a part of `q`. -/
theorem mem_footprint {P : List Place} {q l : Nat} :
    l ∈ footprint P q ↔ l < P.length ∧ isLeaf P l ∧ partOf P l q := by
  simp [footprint, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range]

/-- Footprints depend only on the number of places and on structural parents (§40). -/
theorem footprint_congr {P P' : List Place} (hlen : P'.length = P.length)
    (hpar : parentOf P' = parentOf P) (q : Nat) : footprint P' q = footprint P q := by
  unfold footprint; rw [hlen]; congr 1; funext l
  exact decide_eq_decide.2 (by simp only [isLeaf, partOf, hpar, hlen])

/-- The frame of a place is unique (§40, `placeFrame`). -/
theorem FrameOf.det {s : S3} {q f f' : Nat} (h : FrameOf s q f) (h' : FrameOf s q f') :
    f = f' := by

/-! ## Effective modes (§43) -/

/-- Cases 2 and 4 of §43: a present effective mode is the own mode when no active descendant
covers the leaf, `Observe` when only `Observe` descendants do. -/
theorem effOf_cases {m m' : Mode} {ds : List Mode} (h : effOf m ds = some m') :
    (ds = [] ∧ m' = m) ∨ (ds ≠ [] ∧ Mode.modify ∉ ds ∧ m' = .observe) := by
  unfold effOf at h
  by_cases h0 : ds = []
  · simp [h0] at h; exact .inl ⟨h0, h.symm⟩
  · by_cases h1 : Mode.modify ∈ ds
    · simp [h0, h1] at h
    · simp [h0, h1] at h; exact .inr ⟨h0, h1, h.symm⟩

/-- A mode other than `Modify` is `Observe` (§42). -/
theorem mode_eq_observe {m : Mode} (h : m ≠ .modify) : m = .observe := by cases m <;> simp_all

/-- Membership in `descModes` (§43): the mode of an active descendant covering the leaf. -/
theorem mem_descModes {s : S3} {a p : Nat} {m : Mode} :
    m ∈ descModes s a p ↔ ∃ j y, s.A[j]? = some y ∧ y.active = true ∧ p ∈ y.footprint ∧
      a ∈ s.ancs j ∧ y.mode = m := by
  simp only [descModes, List.mem_filterMap, List.mem_range]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨j, -, h⟩
    split at h
    · rename_i y hy
      split at h
      · rename_i hc; cases h; exact ⟨j, y, hy, hc.1, hc.2.1, hc.2.2, rfl⟩
      · cases h
    · cases h
  · rintro ⟨j, y, hy, h1, h2, h3, rfl⟩
    refine ⟨j, (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 hy).1, ?_⟩
    simp [hy, h1, h2, h3]

/-- A present effective mode (§43, case 1): the authority is active and covers the leaf. -/
theorem effective_some {s : S3} {a p : Nat} {m : Mode} (h : effective s a p = some m) :
    ∃ x, s.A[a]? = some x ∧ x.active = true ∧ p ∈ x.footprint ∧
      effOf x.mode (descModes s a p) = some m := by
  unfold effective at h
  split at h
  · rename_i x hx; split at h
    · rename_i hc; exact ⟨x, hx, hc.1, hc.2, h⟩
    · cases h
  · cases h

/-- The effective mode of an active authority covering the leaf (§43, cases 2–4). -/
theorem effective_eq {s : S3} {a p : Nat} {x : Authority} (hx : s.A[a]? = some x)
    (ha : x.active = true) (hp : p ∈ x.footprint) :
    effective s a p = effOf x.mode (descModes s a p) := by
  simp [effective, hx, ha, hp]

/-- The mode order is reflexive (§43). -/
theorem Mode.le_refl (m : Mode) : m.le m := by cases m <;> simp [Mode.le]

/-- The effective mode does not exceed the own mode (§43). -/
theorem effective_le {s : S3} {a p : Nat} {m : Mode} {x : Authority} (hx : s.A[a]? = some x)
    (h : effective s a p = some m) : m.le x.mode := by
  obtain ⟨x', hx', -, -, he⟩ := effective_some h
  rw [hx] at hx'; cases hx'
  rcases effOf_cases he with ⟨-, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, -, rfl⟩
  · exact Mode.le_refl _
  · simp [Mode.le]

/-- The mode order is transitive (§43). -/
theorem Mode.le_trans {a b c : Mode} (h₁ : a.le b) (h₂ : b.le c) : a.le c := by
  cases a <;> cases b <;> cases c <;> simp_all [Mode.le]

/-- Only `Observe` is below `Observe` (§43). -/
theorem Mode.le_observe {m : Mode} (h : m.le .observe) : m = .observe := by
  cases m <;> simp_all [Mode.le]

/-- A mode permitted by a present effective mode (§43): below the own mode when no active
descendant covers the leaf, `Observe` when no `Modify` descendant does. -/
theorem allows_effOf {m m' : Mode} {ds : List Mode} (h : Allows (effOf m ds) m') :
    (ds = [] ∧ m'.le m) ∨ (Mode.modify ∉ ds ∧ m' = .observe) := by
  unfold Allows OptP at h
  split at h
  · rename_i e he
    rcases effOf_cases he with ⟨h0, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, hn, rfl⟩
    · exact .inl ⟨h0, h⟩
    · exact .inr ⟨hn, Mode.le_observe h⟩
  · exact h.elim

/-! ## Grounding of a right (§43, §63.4, §69.2, §70.3) -/

/-- `HasRight(s, m, q)` holds exactly when some authority grounds it (§43; §63.4, §69.2,
§70.3). -/
theorem hasRight_iff_grounds {s : S3} {m : Mode} {q : Nat} :
    HasRight s m q ↔ ∃ g, Grounds s m q g :=
  ⟨fun ⟨g, hg, he, hl⟩ => ⟨g, hg, he, hl⟩, fun ⟨g, hg, he, hl⟩ => ⟨g, hg, he, hl⟩⟩

/-! ## Consequences of `I1` (§50) -/

/-- Under `I1`, two distinct authorities with present effective modes on a leaf have compatible
effective modes, `Observe`/`Observe` (§50, second paragraph). -/
theorem WF3.deadOf {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {l r : Nat} (h : partOf s.P l r) :
    s.dead l = s.dead r :=
  hw.deadOf_aux (l + 1) l r (Nat.lt_succ_self l) h

/-- A structural parent exists and precedes its child (§49.2). -/
theorem WF3.parent_lt {s : S3} (hw : WF3 s) {i o : Nat} (h : parentOf s.P i = some o) :
    o < i ∧ o < s.P.length := by
  simp only [parentOf] at h
  cases hp : s.P[i]? with
  | none => rw [hp] at h; cases h
  | some pl =>
    rw [hp] at h
    obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hlt, -⟩ := hw.places i pl o hp h
    exact ⟨hlt, lt_of_getElem? hpr⟩

/-- The current frame of a nonempty stack belongs to it (§39, §49.1). -/
theorem top_mem {s : S3} (h : s.F ≠ []) : s.top ∈ s.F := by
  unfold S3.top; cases hF : s.F with
  | nil => exact absurd hF h
  | cons f F => simp

/-! ## Usability (§40) -/


/-- Membership in the children of a place (§63.2). -/
theorem mem_kids {P : List Place} {x r : Nat} :
    r ∈ kids P x ↔ r < P.length ∧ parentOf P r = some x := by
  simp [kids, List.mem_filter, List.mem_range]

/-- A place has no children exactly when it is a leaf (§40, §63.2). -/
theorem kids_nil_iff {P : List Place} {l : Nat} : kids P l = [] ↔ isLeaf P l := by
  constructor
  · intro h r hr hp
    have : r ∈ kids P l := mem_kids.2 ⟨hr, hp⟩
    rw [h] at this; simp at this
  · intro h
    exact nil_of_forall_not_mem fun r hr => by
      obtain ⟨hr, hp⟩ := mem_kids.1 hr; exact h r hr hp

/-- Any fuel at least the index gives the same `corr` (§63.2). -/
theorem corrF_fuel (P : List Place) (src dst : Nat) :
    ∀ n m r, r ≤ n → r ≤ m → corrF P src dst n r = corrF P src dst m r
  | 0, 0, _, _, _ => rfl
  | 0, m + 1, r, h, _ => by
    obtain rfl : r = 0 := by omega
    simp only [corrF]; split
    · rfl
    · split
      · split
        · omega
        · rfl
      · rfl
  | n + 1, 0, r, _, h => by
    obtain rfl : r = 0 := by omega
    simp only [corrF]; split
    · rfl
    · split
      · split
        · omega
        · rfl
      · rfl
  | n + 1, m + 1, r, h₁, h₂ => by
    simp only [corrF]; split
    · rfl
    · split
      · split
        · rw [corrF_fuel P src dst n m _ (by omega) (by omega)]
        · rfl
      · rfl

/-- `corr(src) = dst` (§63.2). -/
theorem corr_src (P : List Place) (src dst : Nat) : corr P src dst src = some dst := by
  unfold corr; cases src <;> simp [corrF]

/-- `corr(r)` for a part other than `src`: the child at the position of `r` among the children
of its parent, under the place corresponding to that parent (§63.2). -/
theorem corr_step {P : List Place} {src dst r p : Nat} (hr : r ≠ src)
    (hp : parentOf P r = some p) (hlt : p < r) :
    corr P src dst r = (corr P src dst p).bind fun p' => (kids P p')[posIn r (kids P p)]? := by
  obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ : ∃ n, r = n + 1 := ⟨r - 1, by omega⟩
  unfold corr
  simp only [corrF, hr, ↓reduceIte, hp, hlt]
  rw [corrF_fuel P src dst n p _ (by omega) (Nat.le_refl p)]

/-- An element found at an index belongs to the list (§63.2). -/
theorem getElem?_mem {l : List Nat} {i x : Nat} (h : l[i]? = some x) : x ∈ l :=
  List.mem_of_getElem? h

/-- The place corresponding to a part of `src` is a part of `dst` (§63.2). -/
/-! ## Dynamic pinning obligations (§74, §75) -/

/-- Leaf `l` is dynamically pinned exactly when an active obligation, of some identity `i`, covers
it (§74). -/
theorem S3.pin_iff {s : S3} {l : Nat} : s.pin l = true ↔
    ∃ (i : Nat) (ob : PinOb), s.pins[i]? = some ob ∧ ob.active = true ∧ l ∈ ob.leaves := by
  simp only [S3.pin, List.any_eq_true, Bool.and_eq_true, List.contains_iff_mem]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨ob, hob, ha, hl⟩
    obtain ⟨i, hi⟩ := List.mem_iff_getElem?.1 hob
    exact ⟨i, ob, hi, ha, hl⟩
  · rintro ⟨i, ob, hi, ha, hl⟩; exact ⟨ob, List.mem_iff_getElem?.2 ⟨i, hi⟩, ha, hl⟩

/-- Dynamic pinning depends only on the obligations (§74). -/
theorem S3.pin_congr {s s' : S3} (h : s'.pins = s.pins) : s'.pin = s.pin := by
  funext l; simp only [S3.pin, h]

/-- After `pin p`, a leaf is pinned when it was, or when it is a leaf of `p` (§74 `ok`
effect). -/
theorem pin_pinEff (s : S3) (p l : Nat) :
    (pinEff s p).pin l = (s.pin l || decide (l ∈ footprint s.P p)) := by
  simp [S3.pin, pinEff]

/-- Element `j` of `l.modify i f` (§75 `ok` effect), proved without classical reasoning. -/
private theorem getElem?_modify' {α : Type} (f : α → α) :
    ∀ (l : List α) (i j : Nat), (l.modify i f)[j]? = if i = j then (l[j]?).map f else l[j]?
  | [], i, j => by rw [List.modify_nil]; split <;> rfl
  | _ :: _, 0, 0 => rfl
  | _ :: _, 0, _ + 1 => by rw [List.modify_zero_cons]; split <;> first | rfl | (exfalso; omega)
  | _ :: _, _ + 1, 0 => rfl
  | _ :: l, i + 1, j + 1 => by
    rw [List.modify_succ_cons, List.getElem?_cons_succ, List.getElem?_cons_succ,
      getElem?_modify' f l i j]
    split <;> split <;> first | rfl | (exfalso; omega)

/-- The obligations after `unpin o`: obligation `o` is inactive, the others are unchanged (§75
`ok` effect). -/
theorem pins_unpinEff (s : S3) (o i : Nat) :
    (unpinEff s o).pins[i]? =
      if o = i then (s.pins[i]?).map fun ob => { ob with active := false } else s.pins[i]? :=
  getElem?_modify' _ s.pins o i

/-- After `unpin o`, a leaf is pinned exactly when an active obligation other than `o` covers it
(§75 `ok` effect: a leaf stays pinned while another active obligation covers it). -/
theorem pin_unpinEff_iff {s : S3} {o l : Nat} :

## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

## 39. Execution Frames

`F` is a nonempty stack of identified, non-duplicate frames. Every frame except the initial frame knows its parent. Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places. The **current frame** is at the top of the stack. `ancestor(f₁, f₂)` means `f₁` is `f₂` or an ancestor of `f₂` in the stack and its call chain.

The base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never exits. An exited frame can neither be the terminal owner of a usable place nor hold an authority that remains active. Frames have semantic existence; no particular runtime representation is required.

## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

A **leaf** is a place with no structural children. `footprint(p)` contains the leaves of `p`, and access rights over a place are evaluated on those leaves. Places transitively owned by a value are not automatically leaves of its `footprint`. A logical unit of the access discipline does not automatically constitute an additional allocation in the elementary memory machine.

A place `p` is **usable** (`Usable(s,p)`) if and only if:

1. `p` exists and is not marked dead;
2. if its owner is a frame, that frame belongs to the stack;
3. if its owner is a place `q`, then `q` is itself usable and the chain terminates at a frame in the stack.

An ownership cycle makes no place usable. `placeFrame(p)` is the terminal frame of this chain when `p` is usable. Structural parts share their parent's owner and death marker. A value may be logically ended by `endUse` without the place that contained it becoming unusable; the substorages it owned may, however, die.

A **root place** has no structural parent. Every **usable** root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner (`RootHeld`). This authority cannot be transferred in isolation; root ownership follows a legal transfer of the owning value when necessary.

## 41. Leaf Initialization States

Every tracked leaf has exactly one of the states `Uninit`, `Init`, or `Moved`.

- `Uninit`: no initialized value available in this leaf.
- `Init`: initialized value, subject to type, representation, and storage obligations.
- `Moved`: value consumed by transfer, inaccessible as its former value.

Aggregates may be partially initialized. Both `Uninit` and `Moved` prohibit ordinary reads, while remaining distinct states for diagnostics and end-of-use obligations. An initialization state creates no access permission.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The ownership graph of statics is acyclic: no static is owned, directly or transitively, by itself. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Main

/-!
# Renaming of identities: core definitions

Foundation of the renaming bisimulation of the access kernel for
`specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.1.md` §49, last paragraph: renamings of place and
authority identities (`Ren`), the relation they induce on places, authorities, pinning
obligations (§74, §75) and states (§38), the order facts carried along runs (`Down`, `SibMono`),
the renamed contract (§48, §80), the renamed operations (§60–§75), and the relation of outcomes
(§58). Generic lemmas on these relations, closed by symmetry.
-/

namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access

namespace Rename

/-! ## Renamings (§49, last paragraph) -/

/-- A renaming of identities (§49, last paragraph): a bijection of `Nat` with its inverse. -/
structure Ren where
  f : Nat → Nat
  g : Nat → Nat
  gf : ∀ i, g (f i) = i
  fg : ∀ i, f (g i) = i

/-- The identity renaming (§49, last paragraph). -/
def Ren.id : Ren := ⟨fun i => i, fun i => i, fun _ => rfl, fun _ => rfl⟩

/-- The inverse renaming (§49, last paragraph). -/
def Ren.symm (π : Ren) : Ren := ⟨π.g, π.f, π.fg, π.gf⟩

/-- Composition of renamings, `π` first (§49, last paragraph). -/
def Ren.comp (π' π : Ren) : Ren :=
  ⟨fun i => π'.f (π.f i), fun i => π.g (π'.g i), fun i => by simp [π'.gf, π.gf],
   fun i => by simp [π'.fg, π.fg]⟩

/-- Renaming of a permutation `τ` of `List.range n` (§49, last paragraph): old `x < n` goes to its
position in `τ`, new `i < n` comes from `τ[i]`; identity from `n` on. -/
def Ren.ofPerm (τ : List Nat) (n : Nat) (h : τ.Perm (List.range n)) : Ren where
  f x := if x < n then τ.idxOf x else x
  g i := if hi : i < τ.length then τ[i] else i
  gf x := by
    have hl : τ.length = n := by simpa using h.length_eq
    by_cases hx : x < n
    · have hm : x ∈ τ := h.mem_iff.2 (List.mem_range.2 hx)
      have hi := List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem hm
      simp [hx, hi, List.getElem_idxOf hi]
    · simp [hx, hl]
  fg i := by
    have hl : τ.length = n := by simpa using h.length_eq
    have hnd : τ.Nodup := h.nodup_iff.2 List.nodup_range
    by_cases hi : i < τ.length
    · have hlt : τ[i] < n := List.mem_range.1 (h.mem_iff.1 (List.getElem_mem hi))
      simp only [hi, dite_true, hlt, ite_true]
      exact (List.Nodup.getElem_inj hnd).1
        (List.getElem_idxOf (List.idxOf_lt_length_of_mem (List.getElem_mem hi)))
    · simp [hi, hl ▸ hi]

/-- The inverse of `π` maps forward by `π.g` (§49, last paragraph). -/
@[simp] theorem Ren.symm_f (π : Ren) (i : Nat) : π.symm.f i = π.g i := rfl

/-- The inverse of `π` maps backward by `π.f` (§49, last paragraph). -/
@[simp] theorem Ren.symm_g (π : Ren) (i : Nat) : π.symm.g i = π.f i := rfl

/-- The inverse of the inverse is the renaming (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.symm_symm (π : Ren) : π.symm.symm = π := rfl

/-- A renaming is injective (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.f_inj (π : Ren) {i j : Nat} : π.f i = π.f j ↔ i = j :=
  ⟨fun h => by rw [← π.gf i, h, π.gf], fun h => h ▸ rfl⟩

/-- A renaming is determined by its forward map (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.ext {π π' : Ren} (h : ∀ i, π.f i = π'.f i) : π = π' := by
  have hg : ∀ i, π.g i = π'.g i := fun i => by rw [← π'.fg i, ← h, π.gf]
  obtain ⟨f, g, _, _⟩ := π
  obtain ⟨f', g', _, _⟩ := π'
  simp only [Ren.mk.injEq]
  exact ⟨funext h, funext hg⟩

/-- A renaming composed with its inverse is the identity (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.symm_comp (π : Ren) : π.symm.comp π = Ren.id := Ren.ext fun i => π.gf i

/-- Mapping by `π.f` then `π.g` is the identity on lists (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.map_gf (π : Ren) (l : List Nat) : (l.map π.f).map π.g = l := by
  simp [List.map_map, Function.comp_def, π.gf]

/-- Mapping by `π.g` then `π.f` is the identity on lists (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.map_fg (π : Ren) (l : List Nat) : (l.map π.g).map π.f = l := by
  simp [List.map_map, Function.comp_def, π.fg]

/-- Membership in a renamed list, read backward (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.mem_map (π : Ren) (l : List Nat) (y : Nat) : y ∈ l.map π.f ↔ π.g y ∈ l := by
  rw [← π.map_gf l, List.map_map]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩; simpa [π.gf] using hx
  · intro hy; exact ⟨π.g y, by simpa [π.gf] using hy, π.fg y⟩

/-- Membership of a renamed identity in a renamed list (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.mem_map_f (π : Ren) (l : List Nat) (x : Nat) : π.f x ∈ l.map π.f ↔ x ∈ l := by
  rw [π.mem_map, π.gf]

/-- The f-form of a membership correspondence gives its g-form (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.mem_iff_g (π : Ren) {L L' : List Nat} (h : ∀ x, π.f x ∈ L' ↔ x ∈ L) (y : Nat) :
    y ∈ L' ↔ π.g y ∈ L := by rw [← h, π.fg]

/-- Universal quantification over all identities, renamed (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.forall_iff (π : Ren) {Q Q' : Nat → Prop} (hQ : ∀ x, Q' (π.f x) ↔ Q x) :
    (∀ y, Q' y) ↔ ∀ x, Q x :=
  ⟨fun h x => (hQ x).1 (h _), fun h y => by rw [← π.fg y]; exact (hQ _).2 (h _)⟩

/-- Universal quantification over corresponding lists (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.forall_mem_iff (π : Ren) {L L' : List Nat} (hL : ∀ x, π.f x ∈ L' ↔ x ∈ L)
    {Q Q' : Nat → Prop} (hQ : ∀ x, Q' (π.f x) ↔ Q x) :
    (∀ y ∈ L', Q' y) ↔ ∀ x ∈ L, Q x :=
  ⟨fun h x hx => (hQ x).1 (h _ ((hL x).2 hx)),
   fun h y hy => by
    rw [← π.fg y] at hy ⊢; exact (hQ _).2 (h _ ((hL _).1 hy))⟩

/-- Existential quantification over corresponding lists (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.exists_mem_iff (π : Ren) {L L' : List Nat} (hL : ∀ x, π.f x ∈ L' ↔ x ∈ L)
    {Q Q' : Nat → Prop} (hQ : ∀ x, Q' (π.f x) ↔ Q x) :
    (∃ y ∈ L', Q' y) ↔ ∃ x ∈ L, Q x :=
  ⟨fun ⟨y, hy, hq⟩ => by
    rw [← π.fg y] at hy hq; exact ⟨_, (hL _).1 hy, (hQ _).1 hq⟩,
   fun ⟨x, hx, hq⟩ => ⟨_, (hL x).2 hx, (hQ x).2 hq⟩⟩

/-- Duplicate-free lists with corresponding members are permutations up to renaming (§42: sets
represented by lists; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Ren.perm_of_mem (π : Ren) {L L' : List Nat} (hnd : L.Nodup) (hnd' : L'.Nodup)
    (h : ∀ x, π.f x ∈ L' ↔ x ∈ L) : L'.Perm (L.map π.f) := by
  have hm : (L.map π.f).Nodup :=
    List.pairwise_map.2 (hnd.imp fun hab e => hab ((Ren.f_inj π).1 e))
  refine (List.perm_ext_iff_of_nodup hnd' hm).2 fun y => ?_
  rw [π.mem_iff_g h, π.mem_map]

/-! ## Generic list and option lemmas -/

/-- A duplicate-free list of `n` identities below `n` is a permutation of `List.range n` (§49,
last paragraph). -/
theorem perm_range_of_nodup {l : List Nat} {n : Nat} (hnd : l.Nodup) (hlt : ∀ a ∈ l, a < n)
    (hlen : l.length = n) : l.Perm (List.range n) := by
  refine (List.perm_ext_iff_of_nodup hnd List.nodup_range).2 fun a =>
    ⟨fun ha => List.mem_range.2 (hlt a ha), fun ha => ?_⟩
  refine Classical.byContradiction fun hna => ?_
  have hsub : l ⊆ (List.range n).erase a := fun b hb =>
    (List.mem_erase_of_ne (fun e => hna (by subst e; exact hb))).2 (List.mem_range.2 (hlt b hb))
  have := List.Nodup.length_le_of_subset hnd hsub
  rw [List.length_erase_of_mem ha, List.length_range] at this
  have : 0 < n := Nat.lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.zero_le _) (List.mem_range.1 ha)
  omega

/-- `flatMap` of pointwise permutations is a permutation (§44: `D(p)` is a set; §49, last
paragraph). -/
theorem perm_flatMap_pointwise {α β : Type} {f g : α → List β} :
    ∀ {l : List α}, (∀ a ∈ l, (f a).Perm (g a)) → (l.flatMap f).Perm (l.flatMap g)
  | [], _ => .nil
  | a :: l, h => by
    simp only [List.flatMap_cons]
    exact (h a (List.mem_cons_self ..)).append
      (perm_flatMap_pointwise fun b hb => h b (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hb))

/-- Positions are kept by an injective map (§63.2; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem posIn_map {f : Nat → Nat} (hf : ∀ i j, f i = f j → i = j) (r : Nat) :
    ∀ l : List Nat, posIn (f r) (l.map f) = posIn r l
  | [] => rfl
  | a :: l => by
    simp only [List.map_cons, posIn, posIn_map hf r l]
    by_cases h : a = r
    · subst h; simp
    · have : f a ≠ f r := fun e => h (hf _ _ e)
      simp [h, this]

/-- Two strictly sorted lists with the same members are equal (§63.2: children in index order;
§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem eq_of_sorted_mem {l l' : List Nat} (h : l.Pairwise (· < ·)) (h' : l'.Pairwise (· < ·))
    (hm : ∀ a, a ∈ l ↔ a ∈ l') : l = l' :=
  List.Perm.eq_of_pairwise (le := (· < ·))
    (fun a b _ _ hab hba => absurd (Nat.lt_trans hab hba) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)) h h'
    ((List.perm_ext_iff_of_nodup (h.imp Nat.ne_of_lt) (h'.imp Nat.ne_of_lt)).2 hm)

/-- A related `some` has a related `some` (§38: components read by index; §49, last
paragraph). -/
theorem optionRel_some {α β : Type} {r : α → β → Prop} {o : Option α} {o' : Option β} {a : α}
    (h : Option.Rel r o o') (ha : o = some a) : ∃ b, o' = some b ∧ r a b := by
  subst ha; cases h with | some h => exact ⟨_, rfl, h⟩

/-- A related `some`, read backward (§38; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem optionRel_some' {α β : Type} {r : α → β → Prop} {o : Option α} {o' : Option β} {b : β}
    (h : Option.Rel r o o') (hb : o' = some b) : ∃ a, o = some a ∧ r a b := by
  subst hb; cases h with | some h => exact ⟨_, rfl, h⟩

/-- Related options are `none` together (§38; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem optionRel_none_iff {α β : Type} {r : α → β → Prop} {o : Option α} {o' : Option β}
    (h : Option.Rel r o o') : o = none ↔ o' = none := by
  cases h <;> simp

/-- Symmetry of `Option.Rel` (§38; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem optionRel_symm {α β : Type} {r : α → β → Prop} {r' : β → α → Prop}
    (hr : ∀ a b, r a b → r' b a) : ∀ {o o'}, Option.Rel r o o' → Option.Rel r' o' o
  | _, _, .some h => .some (hr _ _ h)
  | _, _, .none => .none

/-- Transitivity of `Option.Rel` (§38; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem optionRel_trans {α β γ : Type} {r : α → β → Prop} {r' : β → γ → Prop}
    {r'' : α → γ → Prop} (hr : ∀ a b c, r a b → r' b c → r'' a c) :
    ∀ {o o' o''}, Option.Rel r o o' → Option.Rel r' o' o'' → Option.Rel r'' o o''
  | _, _, _, .some h, .some h' => .some (hr _ _ _ h h')
  | _, _, _, .none, .none => .none

end Rename

open Rename

/-! ## Renamed holders and places (§40, §42) -/

/-- A holder renamed (§40, §42; §49, last paragraph): frames are not renamed. -/
def Holder.ren (π : Ren) : Holder → Holder
  | .frame f => .frame f
  | .place p => .place (π.f p)

/-- A place renamed (§40; §49, last paragraph): parent and owner renamed, `kind` kept. -/
def Place.ren (π : Ren) (pl : Place) : Place := ⟨pl.parent.map π.f, pl.owner.ren π, pl.kind⟩

namespace Rename

/-- Renaming a holder back (§40, §42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Holder.ren_symm (π : Ren) (h : Holder) : (h.ren π).ren π.symm = h := by
  cases h <;> simp [Holder.ren, π.gf]

/-- Renaming holders is injective (§40, §42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Holder.ren_inj (π : Ren) {a b : Holder} : a.ren π = b.ren π ↔ a = b :=
  ⟨fun h => by rw [← Holder.ren_symm π a, h, Holder.ren_symm], fun h => h ▸ rfl⟩

/-- Renaming holders twice is renaming by the composition (§40, §42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Holder.ren_comp (π π' : Ren) (h : Holder) : (h.ren π).ren π' = h.ren (π'.comp π) := by
  cases h <;> rfl

/-- A renamed holder is a place exactly when the holder is (§70.1; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Holder.isPlace_ren (π : Ren) (h : Holder) : (h.ren π).isPlace = h.isPlace := by
  cases h <;> rfl

/-- Renaming a place back (§40; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Place.ren_symm (π : Ren) (pl : Place) : (pl.ren π).ren π.symm = pl := by
  obtain ⟨p, o, k⟩ := pl
  simp only [Place.ren, Holder.ren_symm, Option.map_map]
  cases p <;> simp [π.gf]

/-- Renaming places twice is renaming by the composition (§40; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Place.ren_comp (π π' : Ren) (pl : Place) : (pl.ren π).ren π' = pl.ren (π'.comp π) := by
  obtain ⟨p, o, k⟩ := pl
  simp only [Place.ren, Holder.ren_comp, Option.map_map]
  rfl

/-! ## Related authorities, obligations, places and states (§38, §40, §42, §74, §75) -/

/-- Authorities related by the renaming (§42; §49, last paragraph); footprints up to permutation
(§42: a set). -/
structure AuthRel (π α : Ren) (y y' : Authority) : Prop where
  mode : y'.mode = y.mode
  origin : y'.origin = y.origin.map α.f
  footprint : y'.footprint.Perm (y.footprint.map π.f)
  holder : y'.holder = y.holder.ren π
  active : y'.active = y.active

/-- Pinning obligations related by the renaming (§74, §75; §49, last paragraph); identities
kept, leaves up to permutation. -/
structure PinRel (π : Ren) (ob ob' : PinOb) : Prop where
  place : ob'.place = π.f ob.place
  leaves : ob'.leaves.Perm (ob.leaves.map π.f)
  active : ob'.active = ob.active

/-- Place lists related by the renaming (§40; §49, last paragraph); fresh identities fixed. -/
structure PRel (π : Ren) (P P' : List Place) : Prop where
  len : P'.length = P.length
  get : ∀ q, P'[π.f q]? = (P[q]?).map (Place.ren π)
  fix : ∀ q, P.length ≤ q → π.f q = q

/-- States related by place renaming `π` and authority renaming `α` (§38; §49, last paragraph);
footprints, anchors (§44: a set) and pinned leaves up to permutation. -/
structure SRel (π α : Ren) (s s' : S3) : Prop where
  F : s'.F = s.F
  nF : s'.nF = s.nF
  P : PRel π s.P s'.P
  I : ∀ l, s'.I (π.f l) = s.I l
  Alen : s'.A.length = s.A.length
  A : ∀ x, Option.Rel (AuthRel π α) (s.A[x]?) (s'.A[α.f x]?)
  Afix : ∀ x, s.A.length ≤ x → α.f x = x
  D : ∀ q, (s'.D (π.f q)).Perm ((s.D q).map α.f)
  dead : ∀ q, s'.dead (π.f q) = s.dead q
  pins : ∀ o : Nat, Option.Rel (PinRel π) (s.pins[o]?) (s'.pins[o]?)

/-- Parent links go to smaller identities (§49.2; representation of acyclicity, §49 last
paragraph). -/
def DownP (P : List Place) : Prop := ∀ j o, parentOf P j = some o → o < j

/-- Origin links go to smaller identities (§49.5; representation of acyclicity, §49 last
paragraph). -/
def DownA (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ j o, s.org j = some o → o < j

/-- Parent and origin links go to smaller identities (§49.2, §49.5; §49, last paragraph). -/
def Down (s : S3) : Prop := DownP s.P ∧ DownA s

/-- `π` keeps the order of the parts of every place, their positional field order (§63.2; §49,
last paragraph). -/
def SibMono (π : Ren) (P : List Place) : Prop :=
  ∀ x y p, parentOf P x = some p → parentOf P y = some p → x < y → π.f x < π.f y

/-- The simulation invariant (§49, last paragraph; §57): related states, both with downward
links, and `π` keeping field order (§63.2). -/
structure Sim (π α : Ren) (s s' : S3) : Prop where
  rel : SRel π α s s'
  down : Down s
  down' : Down s'
  sib : SibMono π s.P

/-- Owner-accepted hypothesis of 2026-11-06 on `Satisfiable` (§71, §48; §49, last paragraph): it
does not distinguish states equal up to permutation of footprint, anchor and pin-leaf lists
(§42, §44). -/
def KExt (k : K) : Prop :=
  ∀ p sh s t, SRel Ren.id Ren.id s t → k.Satisfiable p sh s → k.Satisfiable p sh t

end Rename

/-! ## Renamed contract and operations (§48, §60–§75, §80) -/

/-- The contract renamed (§48, §80; §49, last paragraph). `FreeCompat`'s `auth` is opaque
(§70.2); obligations keep their identities (§75); `Satisfiable` (§71) is read on related
states. -/
def K.rename (π α : Ren) (k : K) : K where
  DeclaredDisjoint r r' := k.DeclaredDisjoint (r.map π.g) (r'.map π.g)
  SharedMutable l := k.SharedMutable (π.g l)
  Pinned l := k.Pinned (π.g l)
  ExternalDone o := k.ExternalDone o
  Deallocable p := k.Deallocable (π.g p)
  FreeCompat p a := k.FreeCompat (π.g p) a
  Satisfiable p sh t := ∃ t₀, SRel π α t₀ t ∧ k.Satisfiable (π.g p) sh t₀

/-- Arguments renamed (§60–§75; §49, last paragraph). Shapes are not renamed (§71.1, §72.2:
fresh parents); `auth` is opaque (§70.2); `o` is an obligation identity (§75). -/
def KernelOp.ren (π α : Ren) : KernelOp → KernelOp
  | .derive src region m => .derive (α.f src) (region.map π.f) m
  | .split src rs => .split (α.f src) (rs.map (·.map π.f))
  | .release a => .release (α.f a)
  | .transfer src dst => .transfer (π.f src) (π.f dst)
  | .depend q x => .depend (π.f q) (α.f x)
  | .enter ps ls => .enter (ps.map α.f) ls
  | .exit => .exit
  | .read a ls => .read (α.f a) (ls.map π.f)
  | .write a ls => .write (α.f a) (ls.map π.f)
  | .writeShared a ls => .writeShared (α.f a) (ls.map π.f)
  | .pin p => .pin (π.f p)
  | .unpin o => .unpin o
  | .endUse p => .endUse (π.f p)
  | .free p auth => .free (π.f p) auth
  | .alloc pr ow ls => .alloc (π.f pr) (π.f ow) ls
  | .store a p => .store (α.f a) (π.f p)

namespace Rename

/-- Contracts corresponding under the renaming, `Satisfiable` excepted (§48, §80; §49, last
paragraph). -/
structure KCorr (π α : Ren) (k k' : K) : Prop where
  dd : ∀ r r', k'.DeclaredDisjoint (r.map π.f) (r'.map π.f) ↔ k.DeclaredDisjoint r r'
  shared : ∀ l, k'.SharedMutable (π.f l) ↔ k.SharedMutable l
  pinned : ∀ l, k'.Pinned (π.f l) ↔ k.Pinned l
  done : ∀ o, k'.ExternalDone o ↔ k.ExternalDone o
  dealloc : ∀ p, k'.Deallocable (π.f p) ↔ k.Deallocable p
  compat : ∀ p a, k'.FreeCompat (π.f p) a ↔ k.FreeCompat p a

/-- Outcomes related by the renaming (§58; §49, last paragraph). -/
def OutRel (π α : Ren) : Outcome3 S3 → Outcome3 S3 → Prop
  | .ok t, .ok t' => SRel π α t t'
  | .reject, .reject => True
  | .fail, .fail => True
  | _, _ => False

/-- Outcome relations corresponding in both directions (§58; §49, last paragraph). -/
def StepCorr (π α : Ren) (R R' : Outcome3 S3 → Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ o, R o → ∃ o', R' o' ∧ OutRel π α o o') ∧ ∀ o', R' o' → ∃ o, R o ∧ OutRel π α o o'

/-! ## Generic lemmas on the relations (§49, last paragraph) -/

section
variable {π π' α α' : Ren} {s s' s'' : S3} {P P' P'' : List Place}

/-- Related place lists have related bounds (§40; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem PRel.lt_iff (hP : PRel π P P') (q : Nat) : π.f q < P'.length ↔ q < P.length := by
  have := hP.get q
  constructor
  · intro hq
    rw [List.getElem?_eq_getElem hq] at this
    cases e : P[q]? with
    | none => rw [e] at this; cases this
    | some _ => exact (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 e).1
  · intro hq
    rw [List.getElem?_eq_getElem hq] at this
    cases e : P'[π.f q]? with
    | none => rw [e] at this; cases this
    | some _ => exact (List.getElem?_eq_some_iff.1 e).1

/-- Membership in the place range, renamed (§40; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem PRel.mem_range (hP : PRel π P P') (q : Nat) :
    π.f q ∈ List.range P'.length ↔ q ∈ List.range P.length := by
  simp only [List.mem_range, hP.lt_iff]

/-- Universal quantification over the places, renamed (§40; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem PRel.forall_range (hP : PRel π P P') {Q : Nat → Prop} :
    (∀ y ∈ List.range P'.length, Q y) ↔ ∀ x ∈ List.range P.length, Q (π.f x) :=
  π.forall_mem_iff hP.mem_range fun _ => Iff.rfl

/-- Existential quantification over the places, renamed (§40; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem PRel.exists_range (hP : PRel π P P') {Q : Nat → Prop} :
    (∃ y ∈ List.range P'.length, Q y) ↔ ∃ x ∈ List.range P.length, Q (π.f x) :=
  π.exists_mem_iff hP.mem_range fun _ => Iff.rfl

/-- Symmetry of related place lists (§40; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem PRel.symm (hP : PRel π P P') : PRel π.symm P' P where
  len := hP.len.symm
  get q := by
    have := hP.get (π.g q)
    rw [π.fg] at this
    rw [Ren.symm_f, this, Option.map_map]
    cases P[π.g q]? <;> simp [Function.comp_def, Place.ren_symm]
  fix q hq := by
    have := hP.fix q (hP.len ▸ hq)
    show π.g q = q
    conv => lhs; rw [← this]
    exact π.gf q

/-- Transitivity of related place lists (§40; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem PRel.trans (hP : PRel π P P') (hP' : PRel π' P' P'') : PRel (π'.comp π) P P'' where
  len := hP'.len.trans hP.len
  get q := by
    show P''[π'.f (π.f q)]? = _
    rw [hP'.get, hP.get, Option.map_map]
    congr 1; funext pl; exact Place.ren_comp π π' pl
  fix q hq := by
    show π'.f (π.f q) = q
    rw [hP.fix q hq, hP'.fix q (hP.len ▸ hq)]

/-- Authorities related: footprint membership (§42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem AuthRel.mem_footprint {y y' : Authority} (hr : AuthRel π α y y') (l : Nat) :
    π.f l ∈ y'.footprint ↔ l ∈ y.footprint :=
  hr.footprint.mem_iff.trans (π.mem_map_f _ _)

/-- Symmetry of related authorities (§42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem AuthRel.symm {y y' : Authority} (h : AuthRel π α y y') : AuthRel π.symm α.symm y' y where
  mode := h.mode.symm
  origin := by rw [h.origin, Option.map_map]; cases y.origin <;> simp [α.gf]
  footprint := by
    have := h.footprint.map π.g
    rw [Ren.map_gf] at this; exact this.symm
  holder := by rw [h.holder, Holder.ren_symm]
  active := h.active.symm

/-- Transitivity of related authorities (§42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem AuthRel.trans {y y' y'' : Authority} (h : AuthRel π α y y') (h' : AuthRel π' α' y' y'') :
    AuthRel (π'.comp π) (α'.comp α) y y'' where
  mode := h'.mode.trans h.mode
  origin := by rw [h'.origin, h.origin, Option.map_map]; rfl
  footprint := h'.footprint.trans ((h.footprint.map π'.f).trans (by rw [List.map_map]; rfl))
  holder := by rw [h'.holder, h.holder, Holder.ren_comp]
  active := h'.active.trans h.active

/-- Related obligations: leaf membership (§74, §75; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem PinRel.mem_leaves {ob ob' : PinOb} (hr : PinRel π ob ob') (l : Nat) :
    π.f l ∈ ob'.leaves ↔ l ∈ ob.leaves :=
  hr.leaves.mem_iff.trans (π.mem_map_f _ _)

/-- Symmetry of related obligations (§74, §75; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem PinRel.symm {ob ob' : PinOb} (h : PinRel π ob ob') : PinRel π.symm ob' ob where
  place := by rw [h.place]; exact (π.gf _).symm
  leaves := by have := h.leaves.map π.g; rw [Ren.map_gf] at this; exact this.symm
  active := h.active.symm

/-- Transitivity of related obligations (§74, §75; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem PinRel.trans {ob ob' ob'' : PinOb} (h : PinRel π ob ob') (h' : PinRel π' ob' ob'') :
    PinRel (π'.comp π) ob ob'' where
  place := by rw [h'.place, h.place]; rfl
  leaves := h'.leaves.trans ((h.leaves.map π'.f).trans (by rw [List.map_map]; rfl))
  active := h'.active.trans h.active

/-- Symmetry of related states (§38; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.symm (h : SRel π α s s') : SRel π.symm α.symm s' s where
  F := h.F.symm
  nF := h.nF.symm
  P := h.P.symm
  I l := by have := h.I (π.g l); rw [π.fg] at this; exact this.symm
  Alen := h.Alen.symm
  A x := by
    have := optionRel_symm (fun _ _ hy => AuthRel.symm hy) (h.A (α.g x))
    rw [α.fg] at this; exact this
  Afix x hx := by
    have := h.Afix x (h.Alen ▸ hx)
    show α.g x = x
    conv => lhs; rw [← this]
    exact α.gf x
  D q := by
    have := (h.D (π.g q)).map α.g
    rw [π.fg, Ren.map_gf] at this; exact this.symm
  dead q := by have := h.dead (π.g q); rw [π.fg] at this; exact this.symm
  pins o := optionRel_symm (fun _ _ hy => PinRel.symm hy) (h.pins o)

/-- Transitivity of related states (§38; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.trans (h : SRel π α s s') (h' : SRel π' α' s' s'') :
    SRel (π'.comp π) (α'.comp α) s s'' where
  F := h'.F.trans h.F
  nF := h'.nF.trans h.nF
  P := h.P.trans h'.P
  I l := (h'.I (π.f l)).trans (h.I l)
  Alen := h'.Alen.trans h.Alen
  A x := optionRel_trans (fun _ _ _ hy hy' => AuthRel.trans hy hy') (h.A x) (h'.A (α.f x))
  Afix x hx := by
    show α'.f (α.f x) = x
    rw [h.Afix x hx, h'.Afix x (h.Alen ▸ hx)]
  D q := (h'.D (π.f q)).trans (((h.D q).map α'.f).trans (by rw [List.map_map]; rfl))
  dead q := (h'.dead (π.f q)).trans (h.dead q)
  pins o := optionRel_trans (fun _ _ _ hy hy' => PinRel.trans hy hy') (h.pins o) (h'.pins o)

/-- Related states with the same new frame stack are related (§38, §39; §49, last
paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.withF (h : SRel π α s s') (F₀ : Frames) :
    SRel π α { s with F := F₀ } { s' with F := F₀ } :=
  { h with F := rfl }

/-- An existing authority has a related authority (§42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.A_some (h : SRel π α s s') {x : Nat} {y : Authority} (hy : s.A[x]? = some y) :
    ∃ y', s'.A[α.f x]? = some y' ∧ AuthRel π α y y' :=
  optionRel_some (h.A x) hy

/-- An existing renamed authority has a related authority (§42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.A_some' (h : SRel π α s s') {x : Nat} {y' : Authority}
    (hy : s'.A[α.f x]? = some y') : ∃ y, s.A[x]? = some y ∧ AuthRel π α y y' :=
  optionRel_some' (h.A x) hy

/-- Authorities are absent together (§42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.A_none (h : SRel π α s s') (x : Nat) : s.A[x]? = none ↔ s'.A[α.f x]? = none :=
  optionRel_none_iff (h.A x)

/-- An existing obligation has a related obligation (§74, §75; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.pins_some (h : SRel π α s s') {o : Nat} {ob : PinOb} (hob : s.pins[o]? = some ob) :
    ∃ ob', s'.pins[o]? = some ob' ∧ PinRel π ob ob' :=
  optionRel_some (h.pins o) hob

/-- An existing obligation of the related state has a related obligation (§74, §75; §49, last
paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.pins_some' (h : SRel π α s s') {o : Nat} {ob' : PinOb}
    (hob : s'.pins[o]? = some ob') : ∃ ob, s.pins[o]? = some ob ∧ PinRel π ob ob' :=
  optionRel_some' (h.pins o) hob

/-- Obligations are absent together (§74, §75; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.pins_none (h : SRel π α s s') (o : Nat) : s.pins[o]? = none ↔ s'.pins[o]? = none :=
  optionRel_none_iff (h.pins o)

/-- Related states have related authority bounds (§42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.Alt (h : SRel π α s s') (x : Nat) : α.f x < s'.A.length ↔ x < s.A.length := by
  have := h.A_none x
  rw [List.getElem?_eq_none_iff, List.getElem?_eq_none_iff] at this
  omega

/-- Membership in the authority range, renamed (§42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.mem_rangeA (h : SRel π α s s') (x : Nat) :
    α.f x ∈ List.range s'.A.length ↔ x ∈ List.range s.A.length := by
  simp only [List.mem_range, h.Alt]

/-- Universal quantification over the authorities, renamed (§42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.forall_rangeA (h : SRel π α s s') {Q : Nat → Prop} :
    (∀ y ∈ List.range s'.A.length, Q y) ↔ ∀ x ∈ List.range s.A.length, Q (α.f x) :=
  α.forall_mem_iff h.mem_rangeA fun _ => Iff.rfl

/-- Existential quantification over the authorities, renamed (§42; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SRel.exists_rangeA (h : SRel π α s s') {Q : Nat → Prop} :
    (∃ y ∈ List.range s'.A.length, Q y) ↔ ∃ x ∈ List.range s.A.length, Q (α.f x) :=
  α.exists_mem_iff h.mem_rangeA fun _ => Iff.rfl

/-- `WF3` gives downward links (§49.2, §49.5; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem Down.of_wf3 (hw : WF3 s) : Down s := by
  refine ⟨fun _ _ hp => (hw.parent_lt hp).1, fun j o ho => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨y, hy, hyo⟩ := Option.bind_eq_some_iff.1 ho
  exact hw.origins j y o hy hyo

/-- Field order kept by `π` is kept by its inverse on the related list (§63.2; §49, last
paragraph). -/
theorem SibMono.symm (hP : PRel π P P') (hs : SibMono π P) : SibMono π.symm P' := by
  have hpar : ∀ x p, parentOf P' x = some p → parentOf P (π.g x) = some (π.g p) := by
    intro x p hx
    have := hP.get (π.g x)
    rw [π.fg] at this
    simp only [parentOf, this] at hx ⊢
    cases e : P[π.g x]? with
    | none => rw [e] at hx; cases hx
    | some pl =>
      rw [e] at hx
      simp only [Option.map_some, Option.bind_some, Place.ren] at hx
      cases hpp : pl.parent with
      | none => rw [hpp] at hx; cases hx
      | some r =>
        rw [hpp] at hx; simp only [Option.map_some, Option.some.injEq] at hx
        simp only [Option.bind_some, hpp, ← hx, π.gf]
  intro x y p hx hy hxy
  simp only [Ren.symm_f]
  rcases Nat.lt_trichotomy (π.g x) (π.g y) with hlt | heq | hgt
  · exact hlt
  · exact absurd ((by rw [← π.fg x, heq, π.fg] : x = y) ▸ hxy) (Nat.lt_irrefl _)
  · have := hs _ _ _ (hpar y p hy) (hpar x p hx) hgt
    rw [π.fg, π.fg] at this; omega

/-- Field order depends only on the parent links (§63.2; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem SibMono.congr {P₁ : List Place} (hpar : parentOf P₁ = parentOf P) (hs : SibMono π P) :
    SibMono π P₁ := by
  intro x y p hx hy; rw [hpar] at hx hy; exact hs x y p hx hy

/-- Symmetry of the simulation invariant (§49, last paragraph; §57). -/
theorem Sim.symm (hS : Sim π α s s') : Sim π.symm α.symm s' s where
  rel := hS.rel.symm
  down := hS.down'
  down' := hS.down
  sib := SibMono.symm hS.rel.P hS.sib

/-- The renamed contract corresponds to the contract (§48, §80; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem KCorr.rename (π α : Ren) (k : K) : KCorr π α k (k.rename π α) where
  dd r r' := by simp only [K.rename, Ren.map_gf]
  shared l := by simp only [K.rename, π.gf]
  pinned l := by simp only [K.rename, π.gf]
  done _ := Iff.rfl
  dealloc p := by simp only [K.rename, π.gf]
  compat p a := by simp only [K.rename, π.gf]

/-- Symmetry of corresponding contracts (§48, §80; §49, last paragraph). -/
theorem KCorr.symm {k k' : K} (hK : KCorr π α k k') : KCorr π.symm α.symm k' k where
  dd r r' := by
    have := hK.dd (r.map π.g) (r'.map π.g)
    rw [Ren.map_fg, Ren.map_fg] at this; exact this.symm
  shared l := by have := hK.shared (π.g l); rw [π.fg] at this; exact this.symm
  pinned l := by have := hK.pinned (π.g l); rw [π.fg] at this; exact this.symm
  done o := (hK.done o).symm
  dealloc p := by have := hK.dealloc (π.g p); rw [π.fg] at this; exact this.symm
  compat p a := by have := hK.compat (π.g p) a; rw [π.fg] at this; exact this.symm

/-- `DDSound` (§80, §23) is invariant under renaming of the contract (§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem ddSound_rename (π α : Ren) (k : K) : DDSound (k.rename π α) ↔ DDSound k := by
  constructor
  · intro h r r' hd l hl hl'
    have hd' : (k.rename π α).DeclaredDisjoint (r.map π.f) (r'.map π.f) := by
      simp only [K.rename, Ren.map_gf]; exact hd
    exact h _ _ hd' (π.f l) ((π.mem_map_f _ _).2 hl) ((π.mem_map_f _ _).2 hl')
  · intro h r r' hd l hl hl'
    exact h _ _ hd (π.g l) (List.mem_map_of_mem hl) (List.mem_map_of_mem hl')

/-- Guarded steps with corresponding preconditions and related effects correspond (§58; §49, last
paragraph). -/
theorem guarded_corr {Pre Pre' : Prop} {e e' : S3} (hp : Pre' ↔ Pre)
    (he : Pre → SRel π α e e') : StepCorr π α (Guarded Pre e) (Guarded Pre' e') := by
  constructor
  · intro o ho
    cases ho with
    | ok hpre => exact ⟨.ok e', .ok (hp.2 hpre), he hpre⟩
    | reject hpre => exact ⟨.reject, .reject (fun h' => hpre (hp.1 h')), trivial⟩
  · intro o' ho'
    cases ho' with
    | ok hpre => exact ⟨.ok e, .ok (hp.1 hpre), he (hp.1 hpre)⟩
    | reject hpre => exact ⟨.reject, .reject (fun h => hpre (hp.2 h)), trivial⟩

end

/-- Renaming the arguments by the inverse, then by the renaming, gives the operation back (§60–§75;
§49, last paragraph). -/
theorem KernelOp.ren_symm_ren (π α : Ren) (op : KernelOp) :
    (op.ren π.symm α.symm).ren π α = op := by
  cases op <;>
    simp [KernelOp.ren, List.map_map, Function.comp_def, π.fg, α.fg]

/-- Renaming the arguments, then by the inverse, gives the operation back (§60–§75; §49, last
paragraph). -/
theorem KernelOp.symm_ren_ren (π α : Ren) (op : KernelOp) :
    (op.ren π α).ren π.symm α.symm = op :=
  KernelOp.ren_symm_ren π.symm α.symm op

end Rename

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access
